rows.note: Use 點頭 as the all-purpose verb for nodding, whether agreeing or giving a brief greeting.

example.english: I give a nod to show I agree.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dim2 tau4 biu2 si6 tung4 ji3

rows.note: Use this for the physical head gesture, or figuratively for the nod itself when someone gives approval.

example.english: They gave a nod after hearing me out.
example.jyutping: keoi5 teng1 jyun4 ngo5 gong2 zau6 dim2 tau4

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for general approval, rather than for the physical gesture or official authorization.

example.english: Everyone gave a nod of agreement to the arrangement.
example.traditional: 大家都對呢個安排表示同意。
example.jyutping: daai6 gaa1 dou1 deoi3 ni1 go3 on1 paai4 biu2 si6 tung4 ji3

rows.note: Use this when the approval is an official authorization, especially for a plan or application.

example.english: This application is still waiting for the official nod.
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 san1 cing2 zung6 dang2 gan2 pai1 zeon2

rows.note: Use 打瞌睡 when someone is dozing or gradually nodding off.

example.english: I started to nod off on the bus.
example.jyutping: ngo5 daap3 ce1 daap3 dou3 daa2 hap1 seoi6

rows.note: Use 搖擺 for something swaying or moving up and down rather than a person nodding.

example.english: The buoy seems to nod up and down in the waves.
example.jyutping: go3 fau4 biu1 hai2 hoi2 long6 zung1 jiu4 baai2

rows.note: Use this for a nomination for an award, position, or other honor.

example.english: They got a nod for Best Actor this year.
example.traditional: 佢今年攞到最佳男主角提名。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam1 nin4 lo2 dou2 zeoi3 gaai1 naam4 zyu2 gok3 tai4 ming4

rows.note: Use 點頭示意 when a nod is deliberately used to signal or indicate something.

example.english: When the guard saw me, they gave a nod to signal me to go in.
example.traditional: 保安見到我，就點頭示意我入去。
example.jyutping: bou2 on1 gin3 dou2 ngo5 zau6 dim2 tau4 si6 ji3 ngo5 jap6 heoi3
